newsitem.title: USA: Hormel sees gradual rise in pork supplies.
newsitem.headline: Hormel sees gradual rise in pork supplies.

text.p: Hormel Foods Corp, a meat processor and food company, said Thursday higher than normal pork raw material costs will continue to be a challenge, even though a gradual increase in pork supplies is expected.

Earlier, Hormel reported fiscal first quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, flat with a year ago. Sales rose to $810.3 million from $724.4 million, due in part to higher selling prices for the company's products.
Hormel said that while total tonnage rose only modestly in the first quarter, increases in its branded, consumer-packaged meat and food products more than offset reduced hog slaughter levels.
Joel Johnson, chairman, said grain costs, principally corn, have eased considerably, reducing costs in the future for Hormel's Jennie-O Foods Inc subsidiary.
"However, prices for pork, the company's primary raw material, remain high due to reduced hog numbers and significant increases in industry-wide slaughter capacity," he said.

"The less plentiful pork supplies and continued higher than anticipated costs have squeezed our margins and made it difficult to operate company facilities at optimum efficiency and economy," he added.
In the first quarter, Hormel said, its meat products group saw a 10 percent tonnage gain, due primarily to increased fresh pork sales.
Grocery products recorded a 12 percent rise in tonnage in the first quarter, which Hormel attributed largely to its acquisition late last year of Stagg Foods Inc.
The Foodservice Group saw double-digit branded sales growth in the quarter.

Jennie-O Foods saw "significant' tonnage volume gains in the quarter. Although corn and soymeal costs declined during the quarter, this division did not achieve its customary margins for further-processed turkey products, Hormel added.
Looking ahead, Johnson said, "...the underlying strength of our core businesses, new product introductions and global expansion efforts provide encouragement for the future."
